### Problem: Edit distance {#sec-st-p2-edit}

::: {.p-statement}
Return the minimum number of insertions, deletions, and replacements that turn `word1` into `word2`.

$0 \le n, m \le 500$. On `horse` and `ros` the answer is 3: replace `h` with `r`, delete `r`, delete `e`. On `intention` and `execution` the answer is 5. The empty string into `abc` costs 3.

Source: [LC 72 · Edit Distance](https://leetcode.com/problems/edit-distance/){.solved difficulty="Medium"}
:::

::: {.p-intuition}
Gluing the strings at the left and replacing every mismatch charges 4 for `abcd` into `bcd`. Deleting the leading `a` charges 1, and then every letter matches. The gap can sit anywhere, so the state is the pair of prefixes, and the last column of the alignment is the only decision.
:::

::: {.p-approach}
- **State.** $dp[i][j]$ = edit distance of $s[0..i)$ and $t[0..j)$.
- **Transition.** Equal letters copy the diagonal. Otherwise one plus the minimum of delete $s[i - 1]$, insert $t[j - 1]$, and replace.
- **Base.** $dp[i][0] = i$ and $dp[0][j] = j$. **Answer.** $dp[n][m]$.
:::

The buttons are in order. Each one keeps the previous solution and changes only what that form changes.

::: {.panel-tabset .solution-forms}

#### Recursion

::: {.form-next}
`f(i, j)` is the distance of the two prefixes. An empty side returns the other length. Equal last letters are kept. Otherwise the three operations each cost 1 and leave a smaller pair.
:::

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| renderings: [light, dark]
def draw(ax, p):
    title, inp, steps, final = Traces.get("edit", "rec")
    assert str(final) == "3"
    V.story(ax, p, title, inp, steps, final)
V.show(draw)
```

::: {.panel-tabset group="lang"}
##### Python

```{python}
#| label: st-edit-rec
def edit_rec(a, b):
    def f(i, j):
        if i == 0 or j == 0:
            return i + j
        if a[i - 1] == b[j - 1]:
            return f(i - 1, j - 1)
        return 1 + min(f(i - 1, j), f(i, j - 1), f(i - 1, j - 1))
    return f(len(a), len(b))
```

##### C++

```cpp
int editRec(int i, int j, const string& a, const string& b) {
    if (i == 0 || j == 0) return i + j;
    if (a[i - 1] == b[j - 1]) return editRec(i - 1, j - 1, a, b);
    return 1 + min(editRec(i - 1, j, a, b), min(editRec(i, j - 1, a, b), editRec(i - 1, j - 1, a, b)));
}
```
:::

#### Memo

::: {.form-next}
Store the pair. Equal letters still make a single call. The three-way branch is what the table will flatten.
:::

```{python}

#| renderings: [light, dark]

    title, inp, steps, final = Traces.get("edit", "memo")
    assert str(final) == "3"
    V.story(ax, p, title, inp, steps, final)
V.show(draw)
```

::: {.panel-tabset group="lang"}
##### Python

```{python}
#| label: st-edit-memo
def edit_memo(a, b):
    memo = {}

    def f(i, j):
        if (i, j) not in memo:
            if i == 0 or j == 0:
                memo[i, j] = i + j
            elif a[i - 1] == b[j - 1]:
                memo[i, j] = f(i - 1, j - 1)
            else:
                memo[i, j] = 1 + min(f(i - 1, j), f(i, j - 1), f(i - 1, j - 1))
        return memo[i, j]

    return f(len(a), len(b))
```

##### C++

```cpp
int editMemo(int i, int j, const string& a, const string& b, vector<vector<int>>& memo) {
    if (memo[i][j] >= 0) return memo[i][j];
    if (i == 0 || j == 0) return memo[i][j] = i + j;
    if (a[i - 1] == b[j - 1]) return memo[i][j] = editMemo(i - 1, j - 1, a, b, memo);
    return memo[i][j] = 1 + min(editMemo(i - 1, j, a, b, memo),
        min(editMemo(i, j - 1, a, b, memo), editMemo(i - 1, j - 1, a, b, memo)));
}
```
:::

#### Table

::: {.form-next}
Borders are `0..n` and `0..m`. A match copies the diagonal. A mismatch adds 1 to the best of the three neighbours. Forgetting the replacement term answers the indel distance $n + m - 2 \cdot \mathrm{LCS}$: sample 1 becomes 4, not 3.
:::

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| renderings: [light, dark]
def draw(ax, p):
    title, inp, steps, final = Traces.get("edit", "tab")
    assert str(final) == "3"
    V.story(ax, p, title, inp, steps, final)
V.show(draw)
```

::: {.panel-tabset group="lang"}
##### Python

```{python}
#| label: st-edit-tab
def edit_tab(a, b):
    n, m = len(a), len(b)
    dp = [[0] * (m + 1) for _ in range(n + 1)]
    for i in range(n + 1):
        dp[i][0] = i
    for j in range(m + 1):
        dp[0][j] = j
    for i in range(1, n + 1):
        for j in range(1, m + 1):
            if a[i - 1] == b[j - 1]:
                dp[i][j] = dp[i - 1][j - 1]
            else:
                dp[i][j] = 1 + min(dp[i - 1][j], dp[i][j - 1], dp[i - 1][j - 1])
    return dp[n][m]
```

##### C++

```cpp
int editTab(const string& a, const string& b) {
    int n = a.size(), m = b.size();
    vector<vector<int>> dp(n + 1, vector<int>(m + 1));
    for (int i = 0; i <= n; ++i) dp[i][0] = i;
    for (int j = 0; j <= m; ++j) dp[0][j] = j;
    for (int i = 1; i <= n; ++i)
        for (int j = 1; j <= m; ++j)
            dp[i][j] = a[i - 1] == b[j - 1] ? dp[i - 1][j - 1]
                : 1 + min(dp[i - 1][j], min(dp[i][j - 1], dp[i - 1][j - 1]));
    return dp[n][m];
}
```
:::

#### One row

::: {.form-next}
`prev` is the finished row. `cur[j - 1]` is the insertion (left). `prev[j]` is the deletion (above). `prev[j - 1]` is the diagonal, still the old row, so it has not been overwritten. Swap the rows and continue.
:::

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| renderings: [light, dark]
def draw(ax, p):
    title, inp, steps, final = Traces.get("edit", "row")
    assert str(final) == "3"
    V.story(ax, p, title, inp, steps, final)
V.show(draw)
```

::: {.panel-tabset group="lang"}
##### Python

```{python}
#| label: st-edit-row
def edit_row(a, b):
    prev = list(range(len(b) + 1))
    for i, ca in enumerate(a, 1):
        cur = [i]
        for j, cb in enumerate(b, 1):
            if ca == cb:
                cur.append(prev[j - 1])
            else:
                cur.append(1 + min(prev[j], cur[j - 1], prev[j - 1]))
        prev = cur
    return prev[-1]

assert edit_rec("horse", "ros") == edit_memo("horse", "ros") == edit_tab("horse", "ros") == edit_row("horse", "ros") == 3
assert edit_tab("intention", "execution") == edit_row("intention", "execution") == 5
assert edit_row("", "abc") == 3 and edit_row("abc", "") == 3
assert edit_row("abcd", "bcd") == 1
```

##### C++

```cpp
int editRow(const string& a, const string& b) {
    int m = b.size();
    vector<int> prev(m + 1), cur(m + 1);
    for (int j = 0; j <= m; ++j) prev[j] = j;
    for (int i = 1; i <= (int)a.size(); ++i) {
        cur[0] = i;
        for (int j = 1; j <= m; ++j)
            cur[j] = a[i - 1] == b[j - 1] ? prev[j - 1] : 1 + min(prev[j], min(cur[j - 1], prev[j - 1]));
        swap(prev, cur);
    }
    return prev[m];
}
```
:::

:::

::: {.p-complexity}
**Recursion** is exponential. **Memoisation** and the **table** are $O(nm)$ time and memory. **One row** is $O(nm)$ time and $O(\min(n, m))$ memory. $n, m \le 500$.
:::

::: {.p-edge}
- Either string empty: the distance is the other length.
- Equal strings: the distance is 0, every step a free diagonal.
- One string a deletion away from the other: `abcd` to `bcd` is 1, not 4.
:::

::: {.callout-warning title="Common mistakes"}
- Borders left at 0. Sample 1 then returns 2. An empty prefix is not free.
- The replacement omitted, so the diagonal always costs 1 extra only through insert and delete. That is $n + m - 2 \cdot \mathrm{LCS}$. Sample 1 returns 4.
- A one-row update that reads `cur[j]` as the diagonal. The diagonal is the previous row's `prev[j - 1]`.
:::

**Variants.** Insert and delete only, no replacement, is $n + m - 2 \cdot \mathrm{LCS}$: [LC 583 · Delete Operation for Two Strings](https://leetcode.com/problems/delete-operation-for-two-strings/){difficulty="Medium"}. An adjacent transposition as a fourth operation, used on a pair of letters at most once, adds the cell $(i - 2, j - 2)$ when the two letters are swapped.
